headline: MongoDB Atlas (Posture) onboarding added; the Cloud Posture source list grows to about 100 connectors
summary_md:
- A new **MongoDB Atlas (Posture)** onboarding page lands, and the Cloud Posture and Runtime Security source list expands from 9 entries to roughly 100.
- Twelve **Analytics** pages move out of *Analytics overview* to sit directly under *Analytics*, breaking existing links to the old paths.
- **ITDR** deployment gains a required CyberArk ISP step, and compute units are now documented as consumed by XQL queries only.
- 27 Linux kernel support pages gain 96 kernel builds between them, with none withdrawn.
- Around 30 data source pages get description-only rewording from "data sources" to "data source and connectors", plus a handful of typo fixes.

highlights.title: MongoDB Atlas (Posture) is documented as a Cloud Posture data source
highlights.detail: The new page covers the organization ID and service account client credentials, the generated script to run in the MongoDB CLI, and a regional IP allowlist for accounts behind network policies.

highlights.title: The Cloud Posture and Runtime Security source list jumps from 9 entries to about 100
highlights.detail: It now names AI and SaaS connectors — Claude, ChatGPT Enterprise, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Studio, Gemini Enterprise, Cursor and Generic MCP among them — alongside container registries and SIEM connectors.

highlights.title: Twelve Analytics pages moved up a level, out of Analytics overview
highlights.detail: Analytics engine, sensors, MITRE coverage, Identity Analytics and the whole AI Detection & Response subtree now hang off Analytics directly, so links and bookmarks to the analytics-overview paths break.

highlights.title: ITDR deployment now requires the CyberArk ISP integration
highlights.detail: It is inserted as step 4 of the checklist, and is what collects the audit events the analytics detectors run on.

highlights.title: Compute units are consumed by XQL queries only
highlights.detail: A new note states that agentic and LLM information on the usage page is shown for information and does not draw down the quota.

highlights.title: 96 kernel builds added across 27 Linux support pages, none withdrawn
highlights.detail: Amazon Linux 2023, RHEL, AlmaLinux, Rocky, Oracle Linux, Debian 13, SLES 16, CentOS Stream 9 and Ubuntu 18 through 26 all gained rows; every kernel change in the day was an addition.

items.xsiam/configure-cortex-xsiam/cortex-xsia: New page: onboarding MongoDB Atlas (Posture) with an organization ID and service account credentials, plus an IP allowlist step for network-protected accounts.
The supported list grows from 9 entries to roughly 100 and is retitled "data sources and connectors".
items.xsiam/detect-investigate-and-respond-to-: Adds a step: set up the CyberArk ISP integration, which collects the audit events for the analytics detectors.
items.xsiam/configure-cortex-xsiam/data-manage: States that compute unit consumption currently applies only to XQL queries, and adds an MSSP tenant selection note to the usage table.
items.xsiam/configure-cortex-xsiam/cortex-xsia: Warns that scanning private serverless functions requires downloading and re-running the Terraform template to apply the extra permissions.
items.xsiam/onboard-cortex-xsiam/post-deployme: Adds a note to use the default AWS SQS message queue depth of 256 KB or higher.
items.xsiam/detect-investigate-and-respond-to-: Every link in the Explore analytics list drops the analytics-overview segment after the twelve child pages moved up a level.
Moved out of Analytics overview along with its prompt-log collection subtree; the relative links inside were repointed one level shallower.
items.xsiam/configure-cortex-xsiam/cortex-xsia: Now says Microsoft 365 is added as a third-party data source in Cortex XSIAM rather than in Cortex Cloud Data Security.
The section index gains the new MongoDB Atlas (Posture) entry.
